Appearance/Application bar/bar_project_c.description: Place enabled project fields at the left or centre, independently of the application name. Fields placed together share a single group and long names are clipped inside it.
Appearance/Application bar/bar_project_c.whenToChange: Choose Centre to separate project information from a left-aligned Suhina name.

options.name: Left
options.description: Show project fields on the left.

options.name: Centre
options.description: Show project fields in the centre.

Appearance/Advanced/renderer.summary: Choose the graphics system used to draw Suhina after its next start.
Appearance/Advanced/renderer.description: The renderer draws the application window and controls. GPU uses Suhina’s wgpu graphics path; OpenGL uses its OpenGL path. This preference takes effect on the next application start rather than changing the running window. It does not change the audio engine. A command-line renderer choice can override the saved preference for a launch.

options.name: GPU
options.description: Use the wgpu renderer, backed by the platform’s graphics API. This is the default.

options.name: OpenGL
options.description: Use the OpenGL renderer on the next start.

Appearance/Advanced/renderer.whenToChange: Try the other renderer when drawing or resizing the interface is problematic on your system, then apply it at your next planned restart.

Appearance/Advanced/liquid_panel_strengt.summary: Set the global panel liquid strength.
Appearance/Advanced/liquid_panel_strengt.description: Controls the transparency and edge refraction of the Settings backdrop through the theme tint. A detached Settings window keeps a solid background. This experimental 0–100% slider defaults to 0%, which disables the material. It requires the GPU renderer and Animations on; a high-contrast theme suppresses it. Switching from OpenGL to GPU requires an app restart. A theme with its own liquid overrides uses those values instead; enable Use global liquid settings in its editor to use these sliders. Changes apply live and do not affect audio. Strength controls remain editable without the GPU renderer; values are saved for later. The material itself requires GPU rendering and Animations; switch renderer and restart to see it. These global sliders are disabled while the current theme supplies liquid overrides. Enable Use global liquid settings in the theme editor to edit and apply them again.
Appearance/Advanced/liquid_panel_strengt.whenToChange: Increase this to preview a translucent Settings surface. Keep 0% for a flat surface.

Appearance/Advanced/liquid_track_strengt.summary: Set the global track liquid strength.
Appearance/Advanced/liquid_track_strengt.description: Controls reflections and edge refraction on MIDI and audio track headers. Track labels and controls are painted sharply afterward. This experimental 0–100% slider defaults to 0%, which disables the material. It requires the GPU renderer and Animations on; a high-contrast theme suppresses it. Switching from OpenGL to GPU requires an app restart. A theme with its own liquid overrides uses those values instead; enable Use global liquid settings in its editor to use these sliders. Changes apply live and do not affect audio. Strength controls remain editable without the GPU renderer; values are saved for later. The material itself requires GPU rendering and Animations; switch renderer and restart to see it. These global sliders are disabled while the current theme supplies liquid overrides. Enable Use global liquid settings in the theme editor to edit and apply them again.
Appearance/Advanced/liquid_track_strengt.whenToChange: Increase this to add a reflective coating to track headers. Keep 0% for a flat surface.

Appearance/Advanced/liquid_clip_strength.summary: Set the global clip liquid strength.
Appearance/Advanced/liquid_clip_strength.description: Controls reflections and edge refraction on clip bodies. Notes, waveforms and labels are painted sharply afterward. This experimental 0–100% slider defaults to 0%, which disables the material. It requires the GPU renderer and Animations on; a high-contrast theme suppresses it. Switching from OpenGL to GPU requires an app restart. A theme with its own liquid overrides uses those values instead; enable Use global liquid settings in its editor to use these sliders. Changes apply live and do not affect audio. Strength controls remain editable without the GPU renderer; values are saved for later. The material itself requires GPU rendering and Animations; switch renderer and restart to see it. These global sliders are disabled while the current theme supplies liquid overrides. Enable Use global liquid settings in the theme editor to edit and apply them again. Clip reflections and rims use a gentler optical range than panels to keep dense arrangements readable, including at 100 percent.
Appearance/Advanced/liquid_clip_strength.whenToChange: Increase this to add a reflective coating to clips. Keep 0% for a flat surface.

Theme/Theme/theme.summary: Select, edit and package interface themes and their variants, SVG/PNG controls, meters and native layouts.
Theme/Theme/theme.description: Select a preview card to apply a theme immediately. The active theme has a larger preview. Existing tracks and clips keep their stored colours. Edit current theme opens grouped colour controls with opacity for surface colours; changes save live: colours and other settings are saved in a variant of the theme (Custom, made the first time), never in the theme's own file, so a built-in theme needs no copy for them; moving controls or changing artwork of a built-in theme creates a personal copy. A theme with variants shows a row of swatches under its card, the theme's own values first; select a swatch to use that variant. With a variant in use, the name field renames the variant. Theme settings lists the settings a theme declares itself with @property, each with a control for its type (colour, a number in its range, a choice or checked text), saved in the variant in use. Tracks & clips sets the MIDI and audio colours used for future creations. Surface gradients offers independent Panel, Track and Clip overlays, each with a toggle, direction and 2–8 colour/opacity stops. Gradients work without GPU liquid, but reduced effects and high contrast suppress materials. Liquid inherits the global strengths unless Use global liquid settings is turned off to save per-theme overrides; GPU and accessibility restrictions still apply. Save as new theme creates another copy; Reset changes restores the palette captured on entering the editor and its liquid inheritance. Restore built-in offers Save a copy & restore, Restore without a copy, or Cancel restore; existing custom files remain in the library. More provides New variant (starting from the values in use), Duplicate, Reload, Open folder, Back up and Export template. Dropping a theme file or a zip of themes onto Suhina adds it. Interface changes do not alter audio. Select a numbered stop on the shared colour ramp, or drag it to set its position. Only the selected stop shows colour, position and opacity controls. Add selects the new stop; Remove deletes the selected stop while retaining at least two. Direction is separate below. Colour popups have an opaque background for readability. Controls, meters and toolbar adds continuous, segmented, needle and signal-driven artwork-frame meter appearances; the needle display uses existing dBFS measurements, not calibrated analogue VU. Use editable SVG controls installs original vector examples; Restore standard controls removes overrides. Typed SDK device-panel knobs, dials and buttons use the same SVG artwork while retaining labels, readouts and native parameter gestures. Named device-panel/device-control scopes expose semantic classes and scoped palette/text styling. Custom toolbar layout stores order and visibility in the theme. Right-click the top control bar, choose Edit toolbar, drag labelled modules, then Done; the editor also has visibility checkboxes and move arrows. A customized bar scrolls horizontally when narrow. Edit an SVG control accepts self-contained vector markup and reports invalid artwork. Native CSS applies settings and layout written in the earlier form and reports unsupported declarations: settings go to the variant in use and layout to layout.css. Each theme is a folder: theme.css, its style sheet as its author wrote it, which Suhina reads and never rewrites; variants/NAME.json, values for the theme's settings; layout.css, what Suhina's editors set beyond settings (placements, toolbar, artwork, name); and SVG/PNG resources. Settings are custom properties: a core set every theme has (palette tokens, meter, artwork frame rate, liquid, gradients, background strength, Session geometry) and any the theme declares with @property. A built-in theme's variants are kept in a folder of its id without a copy of its CSS. Changes saved outside Suhina appear within a second, and a save over an unread outside edit of a variant file is refused so the file is kept. Themes saved by earlier versions (JSON, or a theme.css that imports advanced.css) are converted once after a read-back check, keeping the originals in the theme's legacy folder; one that does not read without warnings stays as it is. Reset changes also restores the skin captured on entering the editor. Backups hold each theme folder as it is, variants included; the template ZIP holds an editable theme with an example variant, artwork, CSS, layout and background images. The Theme style sheet section explains theme.css, opens the themes folder and lists the sheet's notices; the sheet is edited in a text editor. Suhina's own style engine with Taffy layout reads it. It computes modern scoped colour, font and radius styles, and Flex/Grid positions for toolbar module ids. Workspace panel ids are panel-browser, panel-main and panel-detail under workspace. Authored layout declarations opt into CSS geometry, preserving native visibility; CSS-owned sizes disable the native browser/detail splitters. Removing the layout rules restores native placement and saved sizes. Bars and floating windows remain host-managed. This adapter is experimental: the host controls toolbar height. A retained native scope tree supports child and sibling selectors, named track, clip, slot and scene roles, and hover/active/disabled/focus for connected controls. Changes publish on the following repaint. Connected panels pass authored text colour, font size and radius to ordinary egui widgets while preserving native defaults elsewhere. Connected surfaces paint linear, radial and conic gradients, including repeating forms, with CSS colour interpolation and transparency. Radial/conic gradients resolve authored origins, radii and angles against each surface and use bounded cached spatial textures. Session, Arrangement, clip and piano editors, bars, shared numeric fields and choice fields pass their scoped styles to ordinary egui widgets. CSS transitions and keyframes animate connected paint properties using the native frame clock. Turning off animations or selecting high contrast suppresses CSS motion. Structure changes restart animations; geometry animation and the reduced-motion media feature are not connected. Connected surfaces also paint bounded inset/outset box shadows with offsets, spread, currentColor and approximate Gaussian blur, using cached textures and native clipping. Some raw controls, transforms and filters still need integration. The Theme style sheet section reports source-line notices for known unsupported effects and font declarations; these notices are not a complete CSS validator. Source is bounded to 128 KiB and 64 nested blocks/functions. Styles without toolbar layout declarations preserve the ordinary bar arrangement; customized bars scroll when narrow. These limits appear beside the editor. Conditional styles stay in the theme's sheet; a variant's values apply over them. Toolbar edit mode preserves the real controls and existing native or CSS layout. Its overlay shows an 8 point snap grid. Done saves module offsets to the theme, Cancel or Escape discards the draft, and entering and leaving without changes preserves the layout. Offsets remain relative to native or CSS anchors and are saved as toolbar offset-<module> declarations in layout.css. Missing SVG roles inherit the embedded Suhina default artwork. Reference SVG files and a pristine default ZIP are created under themes/_defaults. Valid edits to reference SVGs are saved as numbered Suhina Default (modified N) themes before restoring the originals; select the new theme in the gallery to use it. Malformed edits within the resource limit are preserved in a recovery ZIP before restoration. Deleted defaults are recreated from the app. Ordinary user theme SVGs remain directly editable. Portable theme ZIPs include inherited artwork and a shared README.md for human and AI authors, covering what, why, how, when, supported customization and limitations. The native centred toolbar exposes the same module ids as custom layouts; paint-only module rules keep native geometry. Transport controls expose control-play, control-stop and control-record ids. Shared native and SDK button SVG bodies respect CSS corner radii and compose with gradient/shadow layers below their glyphs and labels. Shared native text helpers and SDK vector labels render up to four inherited/currentColor text-shadow layers without changing glyph layout or hit targets. Zero blur uses one draw per layer; blur uses a fixed nine-tap weighted approximation, limited to 32 points and offsets of 256 points. Ordinary egui text that bypasses the helper still needs integration. The dark gloss example in a theme package's examples folder supplies original paint-only metallic gradients, rounded SVG-backed buttons and box/text shadows without reflow. Controls are placed by hand with .control-NAME rules for offsets, dimensions, bottom anchoring and volume direction; matching instances share the rule. The visual placement editor (Edit interface) has been removed for now, while layout moves to plain CSS. Session mixer name, colour stripe, pan, volume and meter support independent placement and sizing; Arrangement name, colour, volume, pan and meter are connected too. A horizontal Session fader changes the rail, cap, scale and drag axis together. MIDI/audio icons use replaceable track.midi/track.audio SVG roles. Track name and body artwork may select raw colour and state variants, with up to 32 contiguous SVG/PNG frames at 1-30 fps (skin.artwork-fps); disabling animations freezes frame zero. SDK device controls, labels and panels use device-<control-id> placement names. Their drawing and hit areas move/scale together while parameter ids and commands remain native. Long/non-ASCII ids get stable bounded names. Native project shortcuts are suppressed while placing controls. PNG control artwork preserves authored colours and alpha; each image is limited to 8 MiB compressed, 4096 pixels per axis and 4 million pixels, with a combined inline-artwork budget of 16 MiB. SVG remains self-contained and does not embed images. Frames meter style selects contiguous meter.frame-0 through meter.frame-31 artwork by the louder measured peak over -70 to +6 dBFS, independently of animation settings and artwork fps. Missing or invalid sequences fall back to native continuous bars. Native clip indication, accessible measurements and click-to-reset remain active. Arrangement fold, enable, automation, input/output routing, send navigation and individual return-slot sends are connected too. Individual sends use mixer-send-1 or arrangement-send-1 and subsequent slot numbers, following native return order. Load compact Session geometry under Native CSS supplies theme-owned track/return/scene widths (64-512 points), slot heights (16-64) and header heights (20-64), saved as the --session-* settings. Use auto to remove an override; absent values retain native defaults. Drawing, scrolling and drop/input targets share the new dimensions. Mixer height retains its existing divider and preference. Session and Arrangement remain separate views; this does not add the separately planned mixer view. Mixer bodies and name surfaces consume their own CSS backgrounds and effects. Meter-vertical and meter-horizontal contain meter-level materials whose gradients stay anchored to the full dBFS scale while native peak/RMS extents and opacity reveal the signal; outset shadows glow around the lit region. Empty rails and segment gaps remain empty. Inline PNG artwork does not prevent applying native CSS edits. Full browser/clip/scene, raw-widget and floating-window placement coverage remains in progress. Fader scale labels/ticks can be placed independently using mixer-volume-scale and styled through fader-scale. Their placement does not change parameter gestures. Compact Session CSS stores pan appearance in the theme through .pan { --suhina-appearance: knob; }. Field forces a numerical pan field; native retains the global preference. This override applies to Session and Arrangement and travels in exported CSS. Meter intensity in the theme editor dims measured ink, artwork and glow from 0-100%, saved as the --meter-intensity setting. Clip warnings, native bar rails and audio measurements stay unchanged. Frame images dim as a whole, including any authored background. This is opacity rather than saturation; gradient and palette colours remain independently editable. Advanced meter-level opacity also applies to native bars, hold marks and needles. Transparent CSS fills suppress native fill fallback. Suhina Sheet is a built-in playful spreadsheet-style theme with green chrome, white cells, compact Session geometry and original SVG controls. Duplicate it to edit its CSS, or export it to get its CSS and all 16 SVG roles together. Suhina Meadow supplies classic blue/cream paper controls over an original generated green-hill image. Its embedded wallpaper and effective SVG controls travel in theme exports; the empty workspace reveals the private image through translucent blue/cream glass panels. Meadow enables liquid strengths of 48/24/12 for panels/tracks/clips; actual liquid requires animations and a supported GPU renderer. Adapters without encoded/linear texture-view aliases retain alpha/CSS materials. Suhina Blocks adds original brown plank CSS, stone-like controls and eight colour-keyed pixel track textures, without a landscape or background PNG. Canonical track-column --suhina-track-artwork: on extends track.body behind Session slots. Empty slots preserve artwork while native hover, stop marks and launch/drop commands remain active. Native custom properties inherit from the nearest authored ancestor.
Theme/Theme/theme.whenToChange: Choose a comfortable theme and, when it has them, a variant, then use Edit current theme to tailor its colours, gradients, liquid and the settings it offers; those changes are kept in a variant, so the theme itself stays as it came. Save a copy before restoring if you want an additional version of your current work.

Theme/Folder/themes_folder.summary: Choose the folder Suhina keeps its themes in and reads them from.
Theme/Folder/themes_folder.description: Every theme you make, duplicate or bring in is a folder inside this one, and Suhina watches it, so a theme edited in another program changes the window within about a second. Choose another folder with Browse, or go back to the default (the themes folder in Suhina's data) with Reset; the path is not typed, so it cannot change by accident. Before anything changes Suhina asks whether to move your themes there. If you agree, it makes a backup of the current themes folder beside it (named with the date and time), moves the themes into the new folder (files the new folder has already are kept) and reads them from there at once. Inside the folder, a theme's own folder may be a link (a symbolic link, or a junction on Windows) to a folder elsewhere. The SUHINA_THEMES environment variable, when it is set, wins over this setting.
Theme/Folder/themes_folder.whenToChange: Change this when you want to edit themes in a folder another program can reach, such as one in Documents. Apps installed from the Microsoft Store may only see their own copy of the app data folder, so a folder outside it lets them edit your themes. It also helps when you keep themes on another drive or share one folder between test builds.

Agents/Agents/agents.summary: Allow an attached AI agent to request access to open projects.
Agents/Agents/agents.description: An agent is an external tool that can inspect and edit a project through Suhina’s command interface. Turning this on enables attachment with suhina-cli mcp --attach. Each connection still requires your approval in Suhina. Approved changes appear in the open projects and project edits can be undone. Turning the setting off disconnects attached agents.

options.name: On
options.description: Allow agents to request a connection; this does not approve a connection automatically.

options.name: Off
options.description: Refuse agent attachment and disconnect existing agents. This is the default.

Agents/Agents/agents.whenToChange: Turn this on when you want an assistant to work in the project you are viewing, then approve the intended connection in Suhina.

Agents/MCP write permissions/mcp_project.description: Allow attached agents to write in the folder of the project they act on, including its subfolders. This is on by default. Turn it off to require an explicitly added folder for writes. An unsaved project has no project folder. This does not restrict exports you choose yourself in File > Export.

options.name: On
options.description: Allow writes in the project's folder and its subfolders.

options.name: Off
options.description: Allow writes only in explicitly added folders.

Agents/MCP write permissions/mcp_project.whenToChange: Turn this off when agents should write only to a separate export folder.

Agents/MCP write permissions/mcp_write_f.description: Choose the folders where attached agents may save projects and export audio. Add folder opens the system folder picker; Remove revokes that folder's grant. Each grant includes subfolders and is saved across restarts. Missing folders grant no access. Agents cannot change these permissions. Revocation applies to new operations and exports still gathering plug-in state, but does not cancel a render already running.
Agents/MCP write permissions/mcp_write_f.whenToChange: Add a destination before asking an agent to export outside your project folder, or to export an unsaved project. Remove folders when access is no longer needed.

Agents/Updates/check_updates.summary: Check once at startup whether a newer build is available.
Agents/Updates/check_updates.description: Suhina asks GitHub about the selected update channel once after starting. A newer build can be offered for you to download; enabling the check does not install or restart anything automatically. Help → Check for updates can still check manually when this is off.

options.name: On
options.description: Make the startup update check. This is the default.

options.name: Off
options.description: Skip the automatic startup check; manual checking remains available.

Agents/Updates/check_updates.whenToChange: Turn this off if you prefer to check for updates manually, for example when working offline.

Agents/Updates/update_channel.summary: Choose the builds offered by the update checker.
Agents/Updates/update_channel.description: An update channel chooses which Suhina builds the checker looks for. Nightly builds follow ongoing development. Test builds are produced for proposed changes and appear as a choice only in Developer mode or when Suhina itself is a test build. Without either condition, the effective channel is Nightly. Checking and installation are separate actions.

options.name: Nightly
options.description: Look for the nightly build. This is the default channel.

options.name: Test builds
options.description: List pull-request test builds for your platform when this channel is available. Downloading one requires signing in through the GitHub CLI.

Agents/Updates/update_channel.whenToChange: Use Test builds when testing a particular proposed change, and return to Nightly for the regular development builds.

Agents/Advanced/developer_mode.summary: Expose test builds in the update channel choices.
Agents/Advanced/developer_mode.description: Developer mode makes the Test builds update channel available. It does not select that channel or download a build on its own. Downloading a test build requires the GitHub CLI and an explicit connection from the update dialog. A running test build already exposes Test builds even with Developer mode off.

options.name: On
options.description: Add Test builds to the channel choices.

options.name: Off
options.description: Keep the usual channel choices unless the running app is itself a test build. This is the default.

Agents/Advanced/developer_mode.whenToChange: Enable this when you have been asked to try a test build for a fix or feature.

Audio/Output/audio_host,audio_device,aud.summary: Choose audio hardware, its driver, timing settings and recording input.
Audio/Output/audio_host,audio_device,aud.description: Driver selects the audio system used to reach your hardware; the listed drivers depend on the platform and build. Each driver remembers its last applied device across restarts, including an explicit Default selection. Choosing Driver restores that device and applies the pair together when it is available. Default and the same host selected by name share this memory. For a new driver or an unavailable remembered device, choose Device, including Default if wanted, before the new driver opens. Until then the current output keeps playing; closing Settings cancels the pending driver choice. Installed ASIO devices stay listed while ASIO plays; restart Suhina after installing a new ASIO driver. Default follows the system choice; a missing chosen output can fall back to the default. Sample rate is the number of audio frames per second; choose a listed rate or Device’s own. Buffer size controls the device buffer where supported, including WASAPI exclusive mode; when labelled Engine block it controls Suhina’s rendering chunks, while the operating system or driver keeps its own device buffer. Smaller chunks alone do not guarantee the same reduction in the latency shown under Now. Exclusive mode applies to supported WASAPI devices and reserves the device for Suhina; other applications are then not heard on it. Input independently selects Off, the default input or a named microphone/interface input on the chosen driver. Input is Off initially. Choosing an input supplies audio to tracks configured to use it; it does not itself arm or record a track. Device changes retain running plug-in instances. If the effective sample rate changes, Suhina stops processing while it reconfigures those instances and updates their latency; it does not reload their presets or editors. A plug-in that refuses reconfiguration prevents the new output from starting and reports an error. A plug-in still loading when the rate changes starts again at the new rate. When changing outputs, Suhina fades the old device to silence before closing it and fades in the first audio on the new device. The shutdown drain is limited to 500 ms if a device stops responding; the change still interrupts audio and cannot prevent a pop generated inside the hardware. Device settings, immediately below Device, opens Control panel… for the matching active ASIO driver. The button is hidden while a driver choice is pending, when another device is running, or with a non-ASIO host. The native panel configures the running instance, not an external defaults editor; opening it does not reload plug-ins. While the native panel is open, output changes and project closing are rejected until it is closed. A rejected output choice restores the displayed selection and does not replace the driver’s remembered device. If the device itself fails to open, the requested choice stays selected for retry; device history is updated only after a successful selection. Switching to another driver after a failed opening preserves the previous driver’s last working device. Buffer size requests a supported processing buffer; it does not describe every internal driver or hardware buffer. Exclusive mode is shown only for WASAPI. If opening a device fails, selecting an available device opens a new stopped audio engine; restarting the application is not required to retry.

options.name: Driver: Default / listed driver
options.description: Use the default audio system or explicitly select one. WASAPI is Windows’ audio system; ASIO uses an interface’s ASIO driver when available. Returning to a driver restores its available remembered device in the same operation.

options.name: Device: Default / listed output
options.description: Use the driver’s default output or a named output device. The list follows Driver. The applied selection is saved separately for each driver.

options.name: Sample rate: Device’s own / listed Hz value
options.description: Keep the device’s preferred rate or request one of its advertised rates. Hz means frames per second.

options.name: Buffer size / Engine block: Default / listed frames
options.description: Use the default render block or a listed frame count. Read the row’s label and note to see whether this also sets the device buffer.

options.name: Exclusive mode: On / Off
options.description: On requests WASAPI exclusive access where supported. Off uses shared access. It does not switch ASIO between shared and exclusive operation.

options.name: Input: Off / Default / listed input
options.description: Off opens no audio input. Default follows the driver’s default input; a named choice uses that input device.

Audio/Output/audio_host,audio_device,aud.whenToChange: Select your audio interface and input before recording. If key-to-sound delay is distracting, inspect Now and try a supported smaller buffer; if underruns increase, try a larger one. Use Control panel… for driver-specific buffer and hardware settings.
